text:
Dark and puckered like a purple carnation,

it breathes, humbly sheltered among moss,

still moist from the love that slowly flows

down her white buttocks to its fringed edge.


Filaments like milk tears

wept, rejected by the monstrous squall,

crossing little clots of pink mud

toward where the slope calls them to lose themselves.


My dream has often joined itself to its suction cup;

my soul, longing for material coitus,

made it its tear duct and dwelling of its weepings.


It is the fainting olive tree, and the mimosa flute;

it is the tube where glorious sweets descend:

feminine Canaan isolated among dampness!

translation.title: Dark and Puckered Like a Purple Carnation...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the deliberately grotesque erotic blazon and its floral-biblical exaggeration.
